about: The 3D overworld (world/overworld/; enabled false brings back the painted map everywhere): one stretch of the travel map (data/travel, Wickermoor Hollow) raised as land on Terrain3D (addons/terrain_3d, MIT). window is the part of the travel map's picture it covers ([x0, y0, x1, y1] in the map's 0-1 positions); size is that window's width in metres (1 world unit = 1 m here, not a 5 ft square: the overworld has no battle grid). Each place's position comes from the travel map; `places` here only says how the land lies round it: lie is hollow (a bowl it sits in), hill (a rise it stands on) or flat, with its radius and depth or rise in metres, and lights (warm lamps a village shows at night). lake is a basin of still water. Roads follow the travel map's roads between places inside the window. trees and plants are the game's own plant models (art/plants) by how many per hectare of woods or open ground. rocks are Poly Haven's scanned rocks (art/sourced/polyhaven_forest).
